strengths: Clear and intuitive core motivation: Using raw 4D motion sequences instead of 2D rendered poses avoids information loss and pixel-level copying artifacts
Strong empirical results on TikTok benchmark: FID-VID of 6.98 substantially outperforms second-best (20.64), with consistent improvements across multiple metrics
Comprehensive experimental validation including thorough ablation studies on key components (motion tokenizer, motion attention, CFG) and systematic codebook analysis
Solid technical execution combining VQVAE tokenization with motion-aware DiT and well-motivated 4D RoPE positional encodings
Good generalization demonstrated across diverse styles (anime, photorealism, pixel art) and character types in qualitative results
Thoughtful dataset curation with multi-stage filtering pipeline to ensure high-quality training data
Good reproducibility with code and supplementary materials provided and clear implementation details
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Primarily combines existing techniques (standard VQVAE, DiT, cross-attention); 4D RoPE is straightforward dimensional extension; motion tokenization via VQVAE is established practice
Very small evaluation benchmark (only 6 TikTok test videos) is insufficient for reliable generalization assessment; single-benchmark evaluation is a major limitation for top-tier venues
Overstated 'open-world' generalization claims contradicted by acknowledged limitations (fails on extreme body proportions, insufficient hand control, cannot support multi-person with different poses)

Evaluation methodology concerns: No user studies despite subjective animation quality; some baselines use numbers from original papers (potential inconsistent evaluation settings); no statistical significance testing or computational cost comparison

Technical justification gaps: Using dataset-wide mean joint positions for 4D RoPE spatial coordinates lacks principled justification; how distribution shift affects different body sizes unclear; distinction from 2D rendering in terms of pixel-level copying not rigorously explained

Limited ablation studies: CFG shows minimal impact on FID-VID yet is used in final model (robustness concern); no comparison with 2D pose rendering using same MV-DiT; no ablation on dataset filtering thresholds; missing comparison to reference network approach
Training data limitations: Only 5K pairs after 83% rejection rate; predominantly single-person dance motion; generalization to other motion types and multi-person scenarios unclear

Incomplete analysis: Only two failure cases shown; no systematic study of when/why method outperforms alternatives; limited motion complexity analysis; inconsistency in baseline results (MimicMotion and second-best both report 20.64)
Reproducibility gaps: Hyperparameter choices (codebook size, code dimension, L1 vs MSE loss) lack justification; some design decisions appear ad-hoc; SMPL estimation error propagation not analyzed
Ethical concerns briefly acknowledged but not thoroughly addressed; only planned safeguards mentioned, not implemented

strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly articulates limitations of 2D pose images (fixed shapes, pixel-level copying, missing 3D information) and proposes sensible 4D motion tokenization alternative
Strong quantitative results on tested benchmark: achieves 6.98 FID-VID vs 20.64 for second-best with comprehensive metric evaluation (FVD, FID-VID, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, FID)
Thorough ablation studies: Table 2 systematically validates key components (quantization, positional encodings) demonstrating clear improvements from proposed design
Impressive qualitative results: demonstrates generalization across diverse styles (anime, pixel art, photorealism), multiple characters, full/half-body scenarios shown in Figures 1, 13-15
Rigorous dataset curation: 5K-clip dataset carefully filtered through shot segmentation, pose uncertainty filtering, and multi-faceted quality assessment (aesthetic, optical flow, blur, OCR metrics)
Reproducibility effort: comprehensive supplementary materials including implementation details, dataset procedures, training curves, failure cases, and codebook analysis (Appendix D)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: VQVAE is standard architecture from prior work, DiT is directly from CogVideoX-5B, RoPE is existing technique, 4D RoPE is straightforward concatenation of 1D axes. Contribution is primarily engineering integration rather than novel methodology

Single benchmark evaluation with suspicious performance gap: only evaluated on TikTok sequences 335-340 (6 sequences). 65% improvement over second-best is unusually large and raises concerns about baseline comparisons, tuning, or metric limitations. No evaluation on other datasets (Fashion, other dance datasets) and critically lacking human evaluation studies

Overclaimed 'open-world' generalization contradicts training data constraints: dataset explicitly excludes multi-person animations with different poses (Appendix B), yet Figures 1 and 14 show multi-character results without explanation of how these are generated. Training is dance-focused with high optical flow filtering, not diverse human motions

Dataset scale and scope limitations undermine generalization claims: 5K final clips is small; domain-specific to dance; unclear performance on general human animation (sports, walking, gestures); fails on non-human figures and extreme proportions (acknowledged in Figure 8, Appendix C)

4D RoPE design concern: uses dataset-wide mean joint positions as spatial reference, potentially dataset-dependent and may not generalize to characters with different body proportions. Paper acknowledges limitation (Figure 8) but provides no solution or alternative approach

Incomplete analysis of core contribution (motion tokenizer): ablation shows removing quantization hurts (9.79 vs 6.98) but lacks comparison with continuous features or alternative tokenization schemes. No analysis of what tokens learn or justification for VQVAE over simpler alternatives
Weak analysis of motion-aware CFG: Figure 7 shows CFG has 'minimal impact' on FID-VID metric despite being presented as key contribution, undermining its importance and necessity

Computational efficiency not discussed: 7B parameters, 8 H100 GPUs training, 8 H100 days, 90 seconds inference per video. No comparison with baselines or efficiency analysis; unclear if large model capacity partly explains performance gap

Fairness of baseline comparisons: MTVCrafter uses large CogVideoX-5B backbone; unclear if other methods use same capacity. Performance gap may partly reflect larger model size rather than proposed method. Missing ablation comparing repeat-and-concatenate reference preservation against reference network approaches

Multi-character results unexplained: Figures 1 and 14 show multiple-character animations but training data explicitly single-person only. How are these generated? Significant unexplained discrepancy between claims and training data

strengths: Novel and well-motivated core contribution: directly tokenizing 4D motion instead of 2D-rendered poses with clear justification for why this enables better generalization and motion understanding

Comprehensive experimental validation: thorough ablation studies (Table 2) systematically validating each component, with particularly strong analysis showing 4D RoPE substantially outperforms temporal-only, spatial-only, and learnable alternatives
Strong generalization demonstrated across diverse scenarios: single/multiple characters, full/half-body, multiple artistic styles (anime, pixel art, photorealism), and robustness to pose misalignment

High-quality dataset contribution: 30K→5K curated motion-video pairs with rigorous multi-stage filtering (shot segmentation, pose uncertainty, aesthetic/motion/blur assessment) addressing dataset quality issues in the field

weaknesses: Limited evaluation scope: only 6 sequences from single TikTok benchmark for quantitative evaluation; no cross-dataset validation on Fashion, UBC, or HD-PG benchmarks raises concerns about generalization claims and reproducibility

Incremental technical novelty: individual components (VQVAE for motion, motion attention for DiT, 4D RoPE extension) represent straightforward applications of existing techniques rather than fundamental innovations
Significant practical constraints: unable to handle multi-person animations with different poses, hand articulation remains challenging, requires accurate SMPL estimation with no robustness analysis

Design choices lack sufficient justification: motion-aware CFG using learnable unconditional tokens is somewhat ad-hoc (and Fig. 7 shows minimal FID-VID impact); using dataset mean joint positions for 4D RoPE is dataset-specific with unclear behavior under distribution shift

Comparison fairness concerns: some baseline results taken from original papers rather than reproduced under controlled conditions; large parameter count (7B) and computational cost (~90s inference on H100) not compared against baselines

Dataset limitations: only 5K training sequences primarily focused on dancing data; acknowledged scarcity of non-human figures and detailed hand supervision; behavior on motion types outside training distribution unclear
Asymmetric RoPE application (3D for query vs 4D for key, Eq. 7-8) lacks clear motivation and theoretical justification for this design choice

strengths: Clear and well-motivated core contribution: direct 4D motion tokenization provides more expressive spatial-temporal guidance than 2D-rendered poses, with convincing intuition and empirical validation

Comprehensive technical system design with thoughtful engineering: differential joint coordinates, rigorous dataset curation, novel 4D RoPE extensions, and motion-aware guidance are all well-justified
Strong experimental results: achieves SOTA on TikTok and Fashion benchmarks with consistent improvements across multiple metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, FID, FVD)
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 2-4) validating each component, demonstrating necessity of discrete quantization, differential motion, 4D MA, and 4D RoPE
Impressive zero-shot generalization to unseen motions, diverse character styles, and non-human subjects (animals, objects), demonstrating practical versatility
Scalability demonstration from 6B to 18B parameters with clear performance improvements, valuable for practical deployment

weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty in individual components: diffusion transformers, RoPE, VQVAE are established; 4D RoPE extension is relatively incremental; novelty lies primarily in combination rather than fundamental innovation
Missing critical user studies: quantitative metrics (FVD, LPIPS) don't capture perceptual animation quality, controllability, or user preferences—essential for character animation evaluation

Dataset diversity and quality concerns: filtering from 200K to 30K videos raises selection bias questions; limited documentation of demographic diversity (body types, ethnicities, ages); single-person extraction limitation not thoroughly addressed
Insufficient computational analysis: no inference time, memory requirements, or efficiency comparisons provided; computational costs critical for practical deployment
Limited failure case analysis: only hand control issues shown (Figure 7); systematic failure mode analysis and boundary conditions needed for comprehensive evaluation

strengths: Well-motivated core insight: Direct tokenization of 4D motion sequences is superior to 2D-rendered pose images. The paper clearly articulates this limitation and demonstrates why it matters.

Technically sound architecture: The 4DMoT design using discrete motion tokens with VQ-VAE quantization is appropriate. The 4D RoPE and motion attention mechanisms are well-designed and effectively integrate motion guidance into the video diffusion model.

Comprehensive experimental validation: Extensive evaluation on two benchmarks with multiple metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, FID, FVD, FID-VID). Thorough ablation studies (Tables 2 and 4) systematically validate each design choice with clear contribution analysis.

Demonstrated scalability: Shows the approach scales from 6B to 18B parameters with only minor architectural modifications, suggesting robustness and practical applicability to different deployment scenarios.

Strong zero-shot generalization: Impressive results on unseen motions, styles, and characters. Demonstrates capability across diverse visual domains (anime, pixel art, photorealism, animals, inanimate objects) beyond just human characters.

Reproducibility and transparency: Detailed architectural specifications, comprehensive training details, dataset curation process clearly described, code and model release promised. Extensive supplementary material with additional ablations and detailed implementation information.

Clear presentation and strong motivation: Well-written paper with effective figures. The method progression is logical and the contribution is clearly articulated. Figure 2 effectively motivates the approach.
Practical validation: Commercial deployment and real-world application availability adds credibility to the practical utility and effectiveness of the approach.
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components: VQ-VAE tokenization, Video DiT architectures, and RoPE extensions are well-established techniques. While their combination is novel, the technical contribution is somewhat incremental beyond the core insight that 4D motion works better than 2D.

Insufficient analysis of underlying mechanisms: The paper demonstrates that 4D works better but provides limited investigation into why. Missing deeper analysis of codebook learned patterns, representation properties, or theoretical justification for the improvements.

Narrow evaluation scope: Evaluation limited to two related benchmarks (TikTok and Fashion), both focused on dance/fashion. No evaluation on fundamentally different motion types (sports, gestures, complex scenarios). No user studies comparing visual quality or controllability vs. baselines.

Acknowledged practical limitations not fully addressed: Hand articulation remains a known challenge (Figure 7). Only one failure case shown with limited analysis of failure modes. The impact of poor pose estimation on practical deployment is not thoroughly discussed.

Missing computational analysis: No discussion of training time, memory requirements, inference speed, or computational efficiency compared to baselines. This information is important for practical deployment decisions.

Dataset reproducibility concerns: Custom-curated 30K motion video dataset requires labor-intensive manual inspection and filtering, limiting reproducibility. While detailed, the curation process involves subjective quality judgments that may not be easily replicated.

Modest improvements in some metrics: While consistent, improvements over baselines are sometimes modest. For example, in Table 1, FVD improvements range from 7-8.5 vs. baseline 9-10. Some FID improvements are only 1-3 points.

Generalization claims could be more precise: Zero-shot generalization is demonstrated only on benchmarks similar to training distribution. No evaluation on truly different domains (e.g., sports vs. dance). The claim of 'unprecedented' generalization is somewhat strong given the scope.
